chapter: Ridgley, La Vida, Piron and the Minstrels
title: Leaving with the Georgia Minstrels and being stranded in El Paso
summary: After a stint back at La Vida, Williams left in February 1936 with the Georgia Minstrels, was stranded in El Paso, and stayed; he knew only Kimberl Dial in the show band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And went back to the La Vida. And stayed there a while, about five or six months. And in 36, February the 15th, 1936, I left here with the Georgia Ministry from the Palace Theater. That's right. I stayed with them from February the 15th until March the 25th. They stranded us in El Paso, Texas. That's right. That's where I got stranded, El Paso, Texas. It made it good for me. Yes. Stayed right now. Right there. Stayed there 16 years.
Made it good for me. Played all that Southwest. Arizona, New Mexico, Texas.
Who was the manager of that Georgia Minstrel? Do you remember anything else about the company? Who else was in the band?

Well, I didn't know nobody in the band but Kimberl Dial. He the one gave me the job because he played with us on the boat after Elliot Taylor taking sick. They sent to St. Louis and got him and the guys, Simon, taking sick too. Simon Moreira taking sick on the boat. And they sent to St. Louis and got Kimberl Dial and Jimmy Johnson, bass and alto. So Kimberl was the only guy that I knew on the show. Yeah. I didn't know none of the musicians. I didn't know. Just got quaming with him afterwards, you know.

No. None of them. Different places. Nothing but showmen. That's all they ever played. Show. How fast were you playing that show music? Oh, we had a regular, you see, it wasn't, he had a mental before that, all men. But when he got here, he took a course line, you see. So we played just like a regular nightclub. Yeah, you see. You know. Of course, the grand finale was fast, you know, when you're going off this last show, last of the show, you know. Grand finale, you see. I'll say final, you know. But outside of that, it was all right. Just like you play. One nightclub, blind.
